newsitem.title: INDIA: India and Russia eye small traders to boost trade.
newsitem.headline: India and Russia eye small traders to boost trade.

text.p: Russia asked India on Thursday to set up trading houses between the two countries to encourage medium and small businessmen increase trade.
Visiting Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov told Indian businessmen there had been a substantial fall in trade between the two former Cold War allies since the fall of the Soviet Union.

"I would propose the setting up of trade houses in each other's capital to provide maximum information and assistance to small and medium traders as that is the only way our trade can make a big leap," Luzhkov said.
He was speaking at a meeting of Indian and Russian businessmen organised by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).

Luzhkov conceded that after the fall of Soviet Union there had been a big slump in trade between the two nations and said the failure to quickly adapt to the changing political and economic atmosphere was responsible for that.
India's trade with the former Soviet republics fell almost 88 percent in 1992/93 (April-March) from levels in 1990/91, after the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

Bilateral trade between India and CIS in 1995/96 stood at 77.08 billion rupees ($2.16 billion). Russia accounted for about 70 percent of CIS imports and 92 percent of CIS exports to India, officials said.
Luzhkov also proposed barter trade with Moscow in machine tools and other equipment, saying Delhi could pay in commodities and goods.
The newly appointed Russian ambassador to India, A.S. Cherniyshev, said fresh efforts were needed to boost trade.
"We should not be looking at an improvement of a few hundred million dollars, our target is to increase it many times. So let us work together," he said.
